title: Rod Shoate: Unanimous All-American Linebacker in 1974
question: Which Oklahoma linebacker was a unanimous All-American on the 1974 national champions?
answer: Rod Shoate, a linebacker from Spiro, Oklahoma, was a consensus All-American in 1973 and a unanimous selection in 1974, when Oklahoma went 11-0 and won the national championship. He entered the College Football Hall of Fame in 2013.
summary: Rod Shoate (OU 1972-74) was a consensus All-American in 1973, unanimous in 1974, and a 2013 College Football Hall of Fame inductee. Read his Sooner story.
body: When fans talk about the great Sooner defenses of the 1970s, Rod Shoate belongs near the front of the conversation. The linebacker from Spiro, Oklahoma, played at OU from 1972 to 1974 and became one of the most decorated defenders in program history.

Shoate earned all-conference recognition in each of his three seasons, 1972, 1973 and 1974. On the national stage he was a consensus All-American in 1973 and then a unanimous All-American in 1974, which means every major selector agreed he belonged on the first team. He was also honored as the Big Eight Defensive Player of the Year, including in 1974, according to Wikipedia's account of his career.

The College Football Hall of Fame credits him with 420 career tackles and says he led Oklahoma in tackles three years in a row. That 1974 season ended with an 11-0 record and a national championship under Barry Switzer, and Shoate finished seventh in that year's Heisman Trophy voting, a rare showing for a defensive player.

The New England Patriots chose him in the second round of the 1975 NFL draft, and he played for them for six seasons before two years in the USFL. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in its 2013 class, a fitting honor for the leader of a defense that helped Oklahoma to a title.
